answer_1.quote: Given a source document X = {x₁,…,xₙ} and the corresponding summary Y = {y₁,…,yₘ}, the goal of this work is to design a metric FFLM measuring the faithfulness of Y based on the foundation model LM …

answer_2.quote: We also implemented the language‑modeling based metric BARTScore and metrics based on probability changes include CoP … We report best results for Rouge‑2, Meteor, BLEU and BERTScore …

answer_3.quote: We also compare with prompting and instruction‑tuning techniques under the same model size … LLaMa‑7B is the vanilla foundation language model used to compute probability changes as a judgment of faithfulness.

answer_4.quote: Human annotators or automatic metrics only need to recognize whether the summary is faithful to the document … human judgments were originally done on the sentence level and aggregated to a Likert‑scale faithfulness rating.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators label each summary as faithful or unfaithful (binary) or assign a Likert‑scale score based on faithfulness criteria.
